title: The exceptional set in Goldbach's problem: the weighted density and optimisation steps
abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the elementary core of the method of J. Pintz, A new explicit formula in the additive theory of primes with applications II. The exceptional set in Goldbach's problem, arXiv 1804.09084v2, 2018, whose Theorem 1 is E of X below X to the power 0.72. Pintz turns zero density theorems for Dirichlet L-functions into explicit bounds through two new steps, which this entry proves. Theorem K, display 4.41, solves the extremal problem of displays 4.37 to 4.39: among decreasing configurations d_1 at least d_2 and so on, with caps d_j at most e_j and a density budget, a maximiser of the sum of e to the B d_j minus e to the C d_j saturates every coordinate before its last active one. The proof is the exchange argument of displays 8.10 to 8.16, done here with the cost in the integral form of display 8.11, and a second theorem adds for an abstract concave cost that the budget is used up exactly and the last active coordinate solves the residual equation 4.42. Theorem J, display 4.36, bounds the weighted excess of zeros by 1 minus xi over 2 Delta; it is proved here from the analytic estimate 7.20, which is a hypothesis. Two Section 9 statements are proved in the repository but are outside this submission's selected Comparator check: the basic inequality 9.4 in the form used in 9.22, and Case 8, where e to the minus 7 lambda plus 2.87 times 10.4 times lambda to the 11/7 is below 1 for 0 below lambda at most 0.04. The zero density theorems, the estimate 7.20, the existence of a maximiser and Theorem 1 are not proved and not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic, Codex by OpenAI and Gemini by Google, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
